page.layout: One column of italic verse, lines indented in stanzas, with the author's initials at the foot right. Running head top left, printed page number top right. No margin notes or footnotes.

p.i: Pulchris tenellas qui studiis valet Formare mentes, qui simul ardua Virtutis occultum recludens Monstrat iter venerandus author.
Qui damna mollis pellit inertia Pranúmque frenat rite Cupidinem: Duros iuuentus ut labores Pro patria tolerare discat:
Qui sancta fidos fœdera coniuges Seruare cogit, commoda seu thori Laudat fidelis, seu pudoris Iura sacri violata damnat:
Qui facta non fert inclita fortium Obliuiones carpere liuidas, Chartisve inornatos sileri Egregios pietate Reges.
Nam cum vaganti frena licentia Ponunt, pudendum cumscelus obruunt Culpásque conantur nocentes Vindicibus remouere poenis,
Fulgens nitenti vertice Faustitas Illustrat urbes, rura Ceres beat, Et larga cornu pleniore Copia fundit opes benignas.
Hanc perge dulci materiem Lyra Aptare, vastos aetheris ut petas

main_text.p: POPPAEE tractus, cui virescet Aonia caput usque fronde.

page.notes: The first stanza opens with an ornamental capital (Pulchris, Qui, Nam, Fulgens, Hanc, Aptare are set with large initials in the scan); the Q and A initials are read as Qui and Aptare. "Pranúmque" and "Culpásque" carry acute accents as printed but are uncertain readings. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout; the italic f-like letters are read as s (studiis, facta, cumscelus, virescet, usque). The poem is set in italic capitals for POPPAEE, which is copied in capitals.
